subject: Meteorology
title: Thunderstorm Life Cycle
description: A micro-lesson that makes Thunderstorm Life Cycle usable.

hook.text: A typical thunderstorm lives only 30 to 60 minutes—but in that short life, it goes through three distinct stages.

buildup.text: In the cumulus stage, updrafts dominate—warm air rises, clouds build, but no rain falls yet.

discovery.text: The mature stage begins when rain falls, creating downdrafts alongside the updraft—this is peak intensity.

twist.text: In the dissipating stage, downdrafts spread out and choke off the updraft—cutting the storm's fuel supply.

climax.text: The gust front from the dying storm can trigger new storms nearby—one storm's death sparks another's birth.

punchline.text: Storms die by drowning their own updraft in cold rain.
